title: Implement pinned CORE evaluation protocol
description:
Implement the pinned 22-task nanochat/DCLM CORE protocol end to end: strict bundle loading and provenance, prompt rendering and model scoring, centered aggregation, deterministic bounded subsampling, standalone base-evaluation integration, and a rough reference comparison artifact.

Plan ticket coverage: EVAL-007 through EVAL-009.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Pin nanochat commit 41865401f73ff1c5321ae53297bceb2b78d4c8b4, scripts/base_eval.py SHA-256 644083a99ded710f677b25168ca76fd0416dc7ef3890d346a72f76a20bb522fe, nanochat/core_eval.py SHA-256 9303997ff17fa48ad5e5730f33b7e79a687cc2a1fdad928666bb63dc3514c51d, and eval_bundle.zip SHA-256 90a7c19e28ee7a52b4f6e1f87658deb9fde7f63deba2379045bdb1fe9ea5d200. Treat the 22-task order, paths, baselines, prompt delimiters, few-shot seed 1234 plus shuffled task index, bounded shuffle seed 1337, truncation, mean-continuation-loss scoring, exact-token LM scoring, and centered formula as nanochat_core_v1. Evaluation reads an explicit local bundle and never downloads or mutates data implicitly. Keep typed bundle/domain contracts, prompt construction, tensor scoring, checkpoint composition, and artifact rendering in separate modules. Full runs cover all task rows; max-per-task runs are deterministically bounded, validate the few-shot pool, and remain visibly non-comparable to full results. Save a deterministic reference-comparison report from the pinned bundle CSVs and never present bounded deltas as full-run rankings.
acceptance_criteria:
- A strict loader accepts exactly the pinned 22-task core.yaml order and supported multiple_choice, schema, and language_modeling JSONL shapes; validates unique labels, safe relative paths, one baseline per task, file identities, and pinned bundle identity; and reports missing or malformed artifacts without network access.
- Prompt fixtures match the pinned nanochat rendering and seeded few-shot selection for every task type; BOS-prefixed tokenization, left truncation, continuation spans, BOS padding masks, mean continuation loss for categorical tasks, and exact-token language-model accuracy are tested on CPU.
- The centered formula is exactly (accuracy - 0.01 * random_baseline) / (1 - 0.01 * random_baseline), rejects non-finite or invalid values, and the aggregate is the unweighted mean over the complete configured task set.
- --eval core works independently and in core,bpb,sample order from one checkpoint; --core-bundle is explicit, --max-per-task uses deterministic seed-1337 subsampling and cannot masquerade as a full run, and failures install no partial report.
- base_eval.json records protocol/version/reference commit and files, bundle/config identities, checkpoint/tokenizer identities, per-task raw accuracy/baseline/centered/counts, aggregate, full versus bounded scope, timing, and max-per-task.
- A deterministic Markdown comparison artifact includes pinned GPT-2 family references from the bundle and clearly labels rough full-run versus bounded/non-comparable results. Tiny fake-bundle and fake-model tests cover success, ordering, truncation, insufficient few-shot pools, malformed data, identity mismatch, and atomic cleanup.

title: Make document-packing planner scale to ClimbMix
description: The default small_45m_3090 config uses the packed loader, but its best-fit epoch planner scans every existing row for every document. On the real 16-shard tokenized ClimbMix set (1,354,752 train documents, 871,904,857 tokens, and 253,183 continuation pieces), startup remained at 100% of one CPU core for more than three minutes with zero GPU use and no first batch; the stack was in _place_best_fit_piece. This makes the shipped production preset operationally impractical and forces a flat-loader override.
design: Preserve the exact deterministic best-fit placement semantics while replacing the linear scan over all existing rows with a capacity-indexed or otherwise bounded lookup. Since row capacity is seq_len + 1, exploit the bounded capacity domain and retain deterministic earliest-row tie behavior. Keep the current implementation or a simple oracle for differential tests.
acceptance_criteria: - Packed plans exactly match the existing reference algorithm for randomized small corpora, oversized documents, equal-fit ties, empty documents, padding rows, and fixed seeds. - Planner complexity does not grow quadratically with the number of documents; a deterministic regression proves existing-row count does not add a full scan per placement. - The 16-shard small_45m_3090 manifest can construct its first train batch in a documented bounded time and memory envelope on CPU, with progress or diagnostics sufficient to distinguish planning from a hang. - Packed loader state/resume, loss masks, continuation context, epoch determinism, and flat-loader behavior remain unchanged. - Focused data/pretraining tests and repository quality gates pass.
notes:
Implementation is review-ready. Summary: replaced the quadratic packed-row scan with a residual-capacity bitset and earliest-row heaps while preserving exact best-fit placement, continuation context, masks, padding, seeded epochs, and state format v2; added deterministic work counters and visible 100,000-document CLI milestones; documented the real production envelope. title: Estimate model size tokens per step and VRAM
description:
Add preflight resource estimates that explain each preset's unique parameter count, exact optimizer-step token budget, and conservative training-memory components before a GPU run starts.

Plan ticket coverage: SCALE-004, SCALE-005, SCALE-006.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Build pure estimators from the resolved config and documented single-process assumptions. Parameter size must deduplicate tied weights and separate trainable/non-trainable values. Tokens per microbatch/optimizer step must share the exact accumulation derivation used by training and distinguish processed model tokens from supervised targets. The VRAM estimate must itemize parameters, gradients, optimizer states, activations, logits/loss workspace, and a labeled allocator/headroom allowance for the configured dtype, batch, sequence, depth, width, and vocabulary. It is a conservative planning estimate, never an allocation guarantee. Expose the structured result in pretrain dry-run and compare it with optional actual snapshots through the foundation memory helper.
acceptance_criteria:
- Smoke, tiny-20M, and small-45M configs produce deterministic unique/trainable parameter counts that agree with constructed tied-weight models and identify embedding-dominated size.
- The token calculator returns device_batch_size * seq_len per microbatch and the exact configured total_batch_size_tokens per optimizer step, rejecting non-divisible or contradictory accumulation settings.
- VRAM output itemizes every documented component and assumption in bytes/MiB, includes explicit headroom, and never labels the estimate as observed usage or silently assumes AMP/activation checkpointing.
- Dry-run prints machine-readable and human-readable resource summaries without allocating the full training graph; JSON values are finite and stable.
- Fake/CPU tests cover tied versus untied weights, dtype changes, batch/sequence scaling, overflow/bad config, and component arithmetic; conditional CUDA comparison reports estimate versus actual without asserting a brittle ratio.
notes:
Implemented config-only GPT parameter estimation with tied-weight deduplication and trainability summaries, exact shared token-budget derivation, conservative itemized VRAM bytes/MiB with explicit dtype/manual-attention/no-AMP/no-checkpointing/no-compile/single-process assumptions, 20%-or-512-MiB allocator headroom, signed-64-bit overflow checks, optional estimate-versus-observed accelerator comparisons, and pretrain machine/human preflight output before model construction. Atomically write a schema-versioned metrics/base_eval.json that records requested/completed modes and full domain results, then pass finalized scalars/artifact paths to the Phase 10 reporting adapter. title: Implement continuation-aware full-document BPB protocol
description:
Implement full_documents_v1 as a separate validation-domain protocol that scores every ordinary validation token and byte exactly once with continuation-aware context.

Protocol elaboration: complete-corpus base BPB.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Build a finite one-manifest validation iterator from the Phase 2 continuation policy: a document's first window starts with BOS, later windows carry the previous ordinary token as context, and only new ordinary tokens plus real document-boundary targets are supervised. Freeze document order, row packing, seed/config, and termination in the protocol version rather than inheriting whichever training loader settings happen to be active. The result exposes the common reference_commit field as null because this is a local protocol, while protocol_id/version and reference_config fully identify it. Publish only val_bpb_full_documents and eval/val_bpb_full_documents.
acceptance_criteria:
- One deterministic finite pass terminates after every validation document and counts each ordinary source token and raw byte exactly once as a target, including documents longer than sequence length and documents spanning shards.
- Carried context and residual padding add processed model tokens but no duplicate nats, counted targets, unique source coverage, or bytes; real BOS boundaries remain zero-byte special targets.
- The shared oversized-document fixture reports full token/byte retention of one and contrasts explicitly with nanochat_compat_v1 crop/discard output without calling that protocol's loader.
- Results require protocol_id full_documents_v1, null reference_commit, frozen local reference_config, and only the full-document metric namespaces; unsuffixed compatibility keys are rejected.
- Tests cover empty/Unicode/exact-fit/residual/multi-shard documents, batch padding, order reproducibility, coverage invariants, and no mutation of the training loader state.

title: Implement pinned nanochat-compatible BPB protocol
description:
Implement nanochat_compat_v1 as an independent validation-domain protocol pinned to the exact upstream procedure needed for comparable unsuffixed BPB metrics.

Protocol elaboration: pinned nanochat-compatible base BPB.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.

Reproduce final-validation-shard document order; tokenize in batches of 128 with BOS prepended; maintain a 1000-document buffer; fill each T+1 row by repeatedly taking the first largest document that fits, otherwise take the first shortest document, copy only its prefix to fill the row, and discard the remainder. Preserve resolved B, T, eval_tokens/steps, buffer, and tie behavior in reference_config. This protocol owns val_bpb and eval/val_bpb and must never call the continuation-aware loader.

- nanochat_compat_v1 records the exact pinned SHA and resolved evaluator config, follows final-shard/row-group/document order, and deterministically matches the frozen reference on ties, refill boundaries, multiple rows, and repeated validation cycles.
- Rows start with BOS, have T+1 tokens before x/y shifting, use first-largest-fit selection, and use first-shortest prefix crop/discard when no full document fits; no continuation from a cropped suffix is evaluated.
- The shared oversized-document fixture proves the exact retained prefix, discarded token/byte counts, processed model tokens, unique source coverage, and retention below one without affecting special-token byte totals.
- Results use only protocol_id nanochat_compat_v1 plus the reserved val_bpb and eval/val_bpb namespaces; no full-document key or loader alias is accepted.
- Network-independent tests vendor only minimal expected fixtures/provenance and compare the implementation with a clear frozen reference oracle; production code does not import nanochat.

Implemented nanochat_compat_v1 pinned to karpathy/nanochat commit 41865401f73ff1c5321ae53297bceb2b78d4c8b4 with immutable hashes for scripts/base_train.py, nanochat/dataloader.py, and nanochat/loss_eval.py. Reproduces final-shard row-group/document order, 128-document tokenization batches, 1,000-document whole-batch refill behavior, first-on-tie largest fit, first-shortest prefix crop/discard, repeated cycles, exact source coverage, and reserved val_bpb plus eval/val_bpb keys without importing nanochat or training loaders. title: Define token-byte BPB accumulation and result contracts
description:
Implement the shared, protocol-neutral bits-per-byte arithmetic and immutable coverage result used by both base-validation protocols.

Plan ticket coverage: EVAL-001, EVAL-002.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Accumulate unreduced cross-entropy nats only where targets are non-negative, explicitly supervised, and map to a positive entry in token_bytes; accumulate raw byte lengths from the same target positions. Keep packing and document-selection policy outside this kernel. Define one immutable result schema containing protocol id/version, nullable reference commit plus resolved reference config, checkpoint/tokenizer/manifest identities, source document/token/byte totals, processed model tokens, counted target tokens/bytes, unique source token/byte coverage, retention ratios, total nats, and BPB. Provide a shared oversized-document conformance fixture that protocol-specific beads consume.
acceptance_criteria:
- A hand-computed toy example matches total_nats / log(2) / counted_target_bytes exactly, including multi-byte tokens.
- Special tokens with token_bytes[id] == 0, targets below zero, explicit padding/loss-mask positions, and carried context positions contribute neither nats nor bytes.
- token_bytes shape/type/range, target bounds, loss shape, non-finite losses, inconsistent coverage, and zero counted bytes fail before a report or tracker record is emitted.
- The immutable result validates identities, non-negative counts, total/unique/retention relationships, and deterministic JSON serialization without non-finite values.
- Chunked accumulation matches one-shot accumulation and restores model mode without changing parameters, gradients, optimizer, scheduler, RNG, or loader policy.
- One shared fixture includes an oversized Unicode document and ordinary/special/masked targets for both protocol implementations to prove against.
notes: Implemented strict one-shot/chunked token-byte BPB accumulation, a side-effect-contained protocol-neutral model evaluator, immutable validated coverage/result JSON contracts, and a shared oversized-Unicode conformance fixture. title: Measure training throughput FLOPs MFU and peak VRAM
description:
Produce reusable domain telemetry for base pretraining from actual optimizer-step work and explicit hardware assumptions, leaving Tracker responsible only for transporting the resulting scalars.

Plan ticket coverage: TRAIN-013, TRAIN-014, TRAIN-015, TRAIN-016.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Extend the shared training-step result with actual supervised/model token counts and a callback-free measured interval. Keep one documented model FLOPs estimator and accumulate total training FLOPs from completed work only. Compute tokens/second from counted tokens and interval duration, and MFU from measured FLOPs/second divided by an explicit recorded peak-FLOPs basis rather than an implicit GPU-name guess. Use the foundation memory helper to reset/sample CUDA peak memory at documented logging intervals. Persist cumulative time/FLOPs through the exact-resume contract and expose one immutable telemetry object for Tracker.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every logged optimizer step can report actual processed model tokens, counted supervised targets, measured training duration, train/tok_per_sec, step and cumulative FLOPs, total training time, and train/mfu from one immutable result.
- Timing excludes validation, sampling, checkpoint I/O, tracker fan-out, and startup warmup by documented boundaries; no synchronize is added per microstep solely for logging.
- The FLOPs formula is unit-tested against hand calculations for tied/untied GPT configs and records its assumptions; MFU requires an explicit finite peak-FLOPs denominator and records that basis with the result.
- CUDA peak memory is reset and sampled at one documented interval boundary through the shared helper; CPU runs omit the CUDA-only metric rather than logging zero.
- Resume restores cumulative time/FLOPs monotonically and the first resumed interval cannot double-count pre-checkpoint work.
- Fake clocks, counters, and CUDA APIs prove exact math and callback exclusion; a bounded training integration verifies the domain values without W&B or mandatory GPU hardware.

Summary: added immutable actual-work telemetry for every GPT optimizer step; counts processed positions and non-ignored supervised targets; uses the documented baseline_gpt_dense_training_v1 forward/backward matrix-multiplication estimator with tied/untied correctness; persists nonzero cumulative FLOPs/time across exact resume; requires an explicit finite peak-FLOPs basis for MFU; samples peak allocated CUDA memory around logged optimizer steps while excluding tracker and callback work; records the RTX 3090 advertised FP32 basis in production presets; and documents all timing/formula boundaries. title: Track compatibility BPB and atomic best checkpoints
description:
Add validation-driven best-checkpoint state to base pretraining, with one unambiguous ranking protocol and resume-safe last, periodic, and best artifacts.

Plan ticket coverage: TRAIN-011.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Use only the unsuffixed val_bpb from the pinned nanochat_compat_v1 protocol to decide best.pt; full_documents_v1 remains recorded separately and can never silently replace the ranking metric. Treat strictly lower BPB as improvement. Save a fully resumable checkpoint atomically only after successful validation, persist current and minimum values for both protocols plus the ranking protocol id, and update best.pt without disturbing last.pt or periodic retention. Resume continues the prior minimum and tie policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- Periodic validation returns immutable protocol-tagged results and best.pt is installed only when nanochat_compat_v1 val_bpb is finite and strictly improves the saved minimum.
- Checkpoint metadata records ranking_protocol_id, current and minimum compatibility BPB, current and minimum full-document BPB when available, validation step, and every normal resume field.
- Equal, worse, failed, partial, or non-finite validation never replaces best.pt; last.pt and step checkpoints continue independently and all installs remain atomic.
- Resume restores the prior minimum and cannot overwrite best.pt until a genuine later improvement; changing the ranking protocol or validation identity is rejected.
- Table-driven fake validation curves plus interruption/restart tests verify artifact contents, tie handling, failure cleanup, and tracker/checkpoint event ordering without a GPU.

title: Optimize regex BPE runtime encoding
description: Replace the production RegexBPETokenizer full merge-table sweep with rank-driven active-pair encoding.
